title: Care Management Holds During Hospital, Facility or Correctional Stays
content:
A Care Management episode goes on hold during a hospital, facility or correctional stay and resumes on return home. The first day on hold is recorded as the hold start date, and it is cleared when the episode resumes.

## Closure after a hold

An episode on hold closes with the closure reason hold expired only after the tier's hold maximum, in calendar days, has fully passed since the hold start date.

- **Clock start:** the hold start date recorded on the episode.
- **Counting:** the hold days are counted in calendar days with the hold start date as day 1.
- **Comparison:** closure is allowed only on a day strictly after the last hold day. The last hold day itself — the day whose number equals the tier's hold maximum — does not qualify.
- **Evidence:** the hold start date and status the system shows for the episode, before the closure is recorded.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

Hypothetical inputs: a tier whose hold maximum is 60 calendar days; hold start date 10 June.

| Date | Hold day number | Time condition for closure as hold expired met |
|---|---|---|
| 10 June | 1 | No |
| 30 June | 21 | No |
| 8 August | 60 (the last hold day) | No |
| 9 August | 61 | Yes |

The same start with a 30-day hold maximum makes 9 July the last hold day (day 30) and 10 July the first day on which the time condition for closure as hold expired is met.

## Abstract statement

With a hold maximum of N days, day 1 is the hold start date, day N is the last hold day, and the first day strictly after the last hold day, on which the time condition is met, is day N plus one.

## Resumption

An episode on hold returns to active status when the member returns home; the hold start date is then cleared.
